aid: Fee waivers available through school counselors for qualifying students.

name: USA Fencing High School All-American Team
deadline: TBD (typically spring each year)
eligibility: High school fencers with competitive fencing achievements
aid: None (honorific recognition)
notes: Selective honorific recognition. Boosts college applications. For rising 11th grader, can pursue this in junior/senior year.

name: En Garde! Fencing - USA Fencing School Program
deadline: Rolling (ongoing program)
eligibility: Schools looking to start fencing programs; students at participating schools
aid: Full program costs covered
notes: For a CT high school student: check if your school participates or advocate to bring it to your school. Great for introducing fencing at the school level.

name: USA Fencing NAC Series (North American Cup)
deadline: Various (registration opens per event; check member portal)
eligibility: Current USA Fencing members in good standing
cost: Varies by event (NAC registration fee + USA Fencing membership)
aid: None (competition - pay-to-play)
notes: NAC series is the primary competitive pathway. CT fencers typically attend NACs in cities like Richmond, Milwaukee, Kansas City, Portland, etc. Critical for national rankings and college recruiting visibility.

name: USA Fencing Regional Events (New England Division)
deadline: Various (check division calendar)
eligibility: USA Fencing members in New England Division
cost: Entry fees vary by event ($10-$50 typical)
aid: None
notes: CT fencers compete in the New England Division (CT, MA, RI, VT, NH, ME). Regional events are more affordable, closer to home, and essential for gaining competitive experience and qualifying points.

name: USA Fencing Membership (Competitive License)
deadline: Annual (renews each season, typically August-July)
eligibility: Open to all
aid: None (membership fee)
notes: Must-have first step. CT high school fencer needs Competitive membership to fence in NACs, JOs, Regionals, and Summer Nationals.

name: USA Fencing Lunge Program (Career Mentorship for National Team Athletes)
deadline: Rolling (ongoing applications via Airtable)
eligibility: Must have worn USA jersey at an international cadet, junior, senior, or para fencing event
aid: Career mentorship, resume coaching, job placement support
notes: For a rising 11th grader: aspirational - goal would be to qualify for Cadet/Junior World Team to access this program.

name: CT State High School Fencing (Interscholastic Fencing)
deadline: Seasonal (typically winter/spring semester)
eligibility: Students at CT high schools with fencing programs
aid: School-based (may have fees or be included in athletic programs)
notes: If the student's high school has a fencing team, this is the most accessible competitive opportunity. CT contact: Carrington Ward. Watch live HS events on NFHS Network.

name: USA Fencing Youth Hub - American Development Model (ADM) Resources
deadline: Ongoing (resource hub, not an application program)
eligibility: Open to all (coaches, parents, administrators, athletes)
aid: N/A - educational resource
notes: Useful resource for understanding fencing development pathways. Links to USOPC ADM resources, coach resources, parent resources.

name: National High School Mock Trial Championship (NHSMTC)
deadline: Varies by state; CT state competition typically held in winter/spring. Qualify through school team.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12); must be part of a registered school team through state mock trial organization
cost: Varies by state; typically $50-200 per student for registration, plus travel for nationals
aid: Limited; NHSMTC offers grants to state organizations; some states have fee waivers
notes: Flagship mock trial competition. CT Bar Foundation runs the Connecticut Mock Trial Competition. Student would need to join/form a school team. Excellent for law interest — directly simulates courtroom advocacy.

name: Connecticut Mock Trial Competition (CT Bar Association)
deadline: Typically October-November registration; competitions run January-March annually
eligibility: CT high school students (grades 9-12); must have a school team with a teacher coach/advisor
cost: Minimal registration fee (typically covered by school or CT Bar Foundation)
aid: CT Bar Foundation provides materials and support; no cost to participate beyond potential team fees
notes: Directly CT-based, local, and highly relevant. Judges are real CT Superior Court judges. Student can participate all 4 years of high school.

name: National Speech & Debate Association (NSDA) - Debate & Speech Competitions
deadline: Ongoing membership; school team registration typically in fall. National Tournament qualification: varies by district.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12) at NSDA-member schools
cost: School membership: ~$25-50/student; National Tournament registration: varies
aid: NSDA offers some need-based assistance for NatTour; many schools cover costs
notes: Nation's largest debate organization. Lincoln-Douglas debate directly connects to constitutional/legal argumentation. Congressional Debate relates to model congress. Strong for law profile.

name: We the People: The Citizen and the Constitution (Center for Civic Education)
deadline: Varies by state; national finals typically in April. School registration in fall.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12) at participating schools
cost: Curriculum materials provided free by Center for Civic Education; competition costs vary
aid: Free curriculum; travel costs for nationals may have scholarship support
notes: Constitutional law focus directly relevant to law interest. Simulated congressional hearings develop legal reasoning. Highly respected program with strong government connections.

name: YMCA Youth & Government (Connecticut) - Model Legislature/Model Congress
deadline: Typically registration in September-October; program runs November-April
eligibility: CT high school students (grades 9-12)
cost: ~$150-300 per participant (includes conference fees, overnight stays)
aid: Some financial aid available through local YMCA branches
notes: Full model government experience. Can serve as 'attorney' arguing before mock Supreme Court — directly connects to moot court / supreme court interests. Connecticut program uses the actual State Capitol.; [DEAD: https://www.ymcact.org/programs/youth-government/]

name: Close Up Foundation - Washington DC High School Programs
deadline: Rolling enrollment; programs run year-round. Summer programs fill early. Apply 3-4 months in advance.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12); US citizenship or permanent residency required
cost: ~$2,000-3,000+ for 1-week program (including hotel, meals, activities). Does not include travel to DC.
aid: Need-based scholarships available for students; Close Up offers some financial aid
notes: Directly relevant to civics/law interest. Students visit Supreme Court, meet with lawmakers, debate constitutional issues. Prestigious reputation. Particularly strong for CT-based students given proximity to DC.; [DEAD: https://www.closeup.org/high-school-programs]

name: Constitutional Rights Foundation (CRF) - Civic Action Project
deadline: Ongoing; CAP is typically integrated into classroom curriculum. Individual programs (mock trial, youth court) have varying deadlines.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12); some programs state-specific (CA-focused but resources national)
cost: Free curriculum resources; competition/program costs vary
aid: Most resources free; travel grants may be available for competitions
notes: Excellent free constitutional law and civics resources. National reach. Mock trial case materials available. CRF's programs build legal reasoning skills.; [DEAD: https://www.crf-usa.org/]

name: Supreme Court Summer Institute (Street Law / SCOTUS)
deadline: Varies; teacher institute applications typically in spring. High school moot court programs have fall deadlines.
eligibility: Primarily designed for teachers/educators; high school programs available through Street Law's classroom resources
cost: Varies by program; teacher institute has tuition + travel costs
aid: Limited; check individual programs
notes: Street Law's Supreme Court moot court materials are free and excellent. Student can research and reenact real SCOTUS cases. Strong for independent legal projects.

name: The U.S. Senate Youth Program
deadline: Varies by state; CT typically holds selection in fall. Contact CT State Department of Education.
eligibility: Current high school juniors or seniors (rising junior qualifies for fall of junior year). Must hold elected student government office. US citizen.
aid: Full scholarship included: all program costs covered + $10,000 undergraduate scholarship
notes: Most prestigious high school civics program in the US. Only 104 students nationally per year. Includes $10,000 scholarship. Indian American representation in such programs is respected. Requires elected leadership position (student council, class officer, etc.).

name: Congressional Youth Cabinet / CT Youth in Government
deadline: Varies by program; typically fall for the academic year
eligibility: CT high school students (grades 9-12)
aid: Free state-sponsored program
notes: Free state-level civics program. Direct exposure to CT state government. Can supplement paid programs. Excellent for demonstrating local civic engagement.

name: National Youth Court / Teen Court Programs
deadline: Varies by location; training typically held at the start of school year or semester
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12); must complete training program
aid: Free

name: APIA Scholars (Asian & Pacific Islander American Scholarship)

notes: Not currently applicable for 10th/11th graders, but good to be aware of as a CT-specific opportunity for future planning.; [DEAD: https://www.ctohe.org/scholarships/]

name: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO / USA Biolympiad)
deadline: Open Exam: First week of February annually (school registration earlier). Semifinal: ~March. National Finals: May/June.
eligibility: All US high school students (grades 9-12).
aid: Travel and lodging for National Finals covered by CEE for finalists.
notes: Nearly 10,000 students compete annually. Top 4 gold medalists represent USA at IBO. Team USA has won multiple IBO gold medals. Strongly recommended for biology-interested students. USABO is one of the most prestigious biology competitions for college admissions.

name: AMC 10 (American Mathematics Competition)
deadline: Early Bird Registration: September 30, 2026 ($55 school reg). Regular Registration: October 15, 2026 ($75). Late Registration: October 28, 2026 ($115). Competition A: November 2026. Competition B: November 2026.
eligibility: Students in grade 10 or below. Must be under 17.5 years old on competition day.
cost: ~$30 per bundle of 10 student licenses. Individual cost minimal, typically covered by school.
aid: No direct aid; fee typically covered by school.
notes: Top AMC 10 scorers qualify for AIME. Exceptional AIME performers can qualify for USAJMO. AMC is a key credential for STEM college applications.

name: Science Olympiad
deadline: Season runs September-April (regional/state). National Tournament in May. Membership for 2026-27 opens summer/fall 2026. Join through state chapter.
eligibility: High school students in grades 9-12 (Division C). Must be on a registered school team.
cost: Membership fees vary by state chapter (typically $100-400/school team). Individual cost is minimal through school team.
aid: Limited scholarships available through state chapters and Urban Schools Initiative.
notes: Strongly recommended for biology-interested students. Offers biology events: Anatomy & Physiology, Disease Detectives, Ecology, Experimental Design, etc. 2027 Event Slate released. Demonstrates depth in STEM and teamwork.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
deadline: Affiliated fairs held Jan-March annually. ISEF in May. Must qualify through a Society-affiliated fair first.
eligibility: High school students (grades 9-12) who qualify through a Society-affiliated science fair.
cost: No direct cost to compete at ISEF. Travel/lodging for finalists typically covered by sponsors.
aid: Over $7 million in awards including $100,000 top prize. Finalists receive travel support.
notes: Most prestigious high school science competition globally. Requires original independent research. Highly recommended for biology-interested students. Starting research in 11th grade allows time for meaningful work by spring of 11th or 12th grade.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
deadline: Typically December (RSI 2026 applications now closed; 2027 TBA)
eligibility: High school juniors only; strong academic record; demonstrated interest in STEM research
aid: Full program is free; no tuition cost
notes: Highly selective — one of the most prestigious summer programs in the US. Held at MIT. Requires recommendation letters, standardized test scores, essays, and transcripts. Applications typically open in October.

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
deadline: Typically February (check SSP International site for 2027 dates)
eligibility: High school juniors only; demonstrated aptitude in science and math
cost: Tuition-based; need-based financial aid available. Historically ~$4,000-$6,000 range.
aid: Need-based financial aid available; clothing stipends provided as part of financial aid. Contact admissions@ssp.org for accommodations.
notes: Founded in 1959. Held at multiple university campuses. Extremely selective. 60+ hours/week on research. SSP provides laptops for participants.

name: BU Research in Science & Engineering (RISE) Internship/Practicum
deadline: Typically early February (RISE 2026 deadline has passed; check for 2027 dates)
eligibility: Domestic students currently in junior year of high school
cost: Approximately $11,000+ (tuition + housing/dining). Application fee and $1,000 nonrefundable deposit required.
aid: Limited need-based financial aid available. John Snyder and Phyllis Snyder BU IMPACTS Scholarship available for RISE students with demonstrated need.
notes: 45-year-old program. Students present research at Poster Symposium. Practicum track offers Computational Neurobiology or Data Science. Laptop required for Practicum track.

name: Harvard Pre-College Summer Program
deadline: Early Application & Priority Financial Aid ~January; Regular ~February; Late ~April 1 (for Summer 2027, application likely opens December 2026)
eligibility: Rising juniors and seniors graduating in 2027 or 2028; at least 16 years old by June 20 of program year; not turning 19 before July 31
cost: $6,100 (includes tuition, room, meals, program fee, insurance) + $75 application fee
aid: Limited need-based scholarships available for US citizens/permanent residents/DACA recipients. Awards cover portion of cost, not full amount.
notes: Three 2-week sessions available. No letter grades — ideal for exploring interests. Law, Politics, Philosophy, and History category available. Also STEAM courses. Social activities include trips to Cape Cod and Boston.

name: Harvard Secondary School Program (SSP)
deadline: Early Application & Priority Financial Aid ~January; Regular ~February; Late ~April 1 (Summer 2027 application likely opens December 2026)
eligibility: High school students graduating in 2027 or 2028; age requirements apply
cost: $4,180–$15,735 (depending on program length and format) + $75 application fee
aid: Need-based scholarships available for US citizens/permanent residents/DACA recipients
notes: Earn college credit. Over 200 courses. Biology, molecular biology, neuroscience, and law courses available. Harvard faculty instructors. Visa sponsorship available for international students in on-campus programs.

name: Yale Summer Session (Courses for Credit)
deadline: Rolling admission; early application recommended (Summer 2026 applications are open; 2027 TBA)
eligibility: High school students who have completed 10th grade; visiting students welcome
cost: ~$4,700+ per 1-credit course (tuition only) + residential fees (~$3,600-$4,500 for housing/meals) + $75 application fee + health insurance if applicable
aid: Financial assistance available; need-based
notes: Ideal for earning Yale college credit. Courses in biology, political science, law related topics available. Residential option available in Yale residential colleges. Program in Politics covers pressing issues and global perspectives.

name: National Institutes of Health (NIH) High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP)
deadline: Typically mid-February (check NIH website for 2027 dates)
eligibility: High school students at least 16 years old; US citizens or permanent residents; strong academic record
aid: Stipend provided to cover living expenses. Housing not provided. Students responsible for own housing/transportation.
